title: OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, tool/function calls, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for streaming, tool/function calling, roles, stop/logprobs, and response formatting. Improves streaming stability and aligns SDK behavior with OpenAI compatibility layer.
description:
Motivation: Customers relying on the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions endpoint expect parity in behavior for streaming, tool/function calling, role handling, stop tokens, logprobs, and final response formatting. Multiple downstream SDKs and third-party tools depend on subtle OpenAI semantics (system/user/assistant roles, stop handling, logprob attachment, and chunked streaming frames) which Redwood's current compatibility layer did not fully match. This PR implements parity fixes and streaming stability improvements, with tests and updated docs.

What this PR does: 1) Streaming stability: tighten framing rules for streaming chunks to ensure finalization messages are emitted exactly once and partial delta aggregation is consistent with OpenAI semantics. Added backpressure-safe flushing to avoid dropped final tokens under high-concurrency workloads. 2) Tool/function calling: extend the compatibility layer to serialize/deserialize function call objects the same way OpenAI does; include name, arguments (stringified JSON) and allow the assistant to trigger calls mid-stream. 3) Roles: normalize role names from input (e.g., 'system'/'user'/'assistant' case-insensitive) and preserve role tokens in streaming deltas. 4) stop/logprobs: support 'stop' as string or list of strings in both sync and streaming paths; attach token-level logprobs to completed choices when a model exposes logprobs, and ensure they are present in the final non-streaming response and emitted as final frames in streaming mode. 5) Response formatting: align choice indexing, finish_reason values, and message content shaping (content vs structured fields) with OpenAI's documented responses.

Files changed (high-level):  - runtime/streaming/frame_encoder.py: adjust frame emission ordering and flushing logic (small, focused changes).  - runtime/compat/openai_api.py: add new parity helpers for function_call serialization, role normalization, and stop handling.  - api/handlers/chat_completions.py: wire compatibility layer into both streaming and non-streaming paths; small changes to how choices are assembled.  - tests/integration/test_chat_parity.py: new integration tests covering streaming finalization, function call frames, stop sequences, and logprobs attachment.  - docs/openai_compat.md: document updated differences and examples for function calls and streaming.  - sdk/python/openai_compat_examples.py: example usage updated to show tool calling in streaming mode.

Commits (summary):  - 3c4f20a: initial implementation of role normalization and stop list handling.  - a9b1d3e: streaming frame ordering and finalization fix; add flush/backpressure guard.  - f4e7b21: function call serialization + streaming frames for tool triggers.  - d2b6b90: attach logprobs to final choice object and emit final logprob frame in streaming.  - e8a3c4f: tests and docs updates.

Testing: Expanded integration coverage to include: multi-choice streaming, nested function call arguments, mixed stop tokens, and models that emit logprobs. Locally ran full CI; CI flaked on an unrelated flaky test (slo-toolkit / trace-export) on first run, then passed after rerun. Performance: microbenchmarks show <2% latency increase in non-streaming path and negligible throughput impact for our primary CPU/GPU profiles.

Review highlights and conversation: 
- Alex Kim: "Left a couple of nits around the frame encoder API and a question about how we serialize large function arguments (should we stream those separately?). Also please add an example showing function calls in the python SDK docs." 
- Priya (author): "Addressed the encoder nit and added chunked function-arg support with a size cap + fallback to payload reference. Added python example in the docs." 
- Daniel Soto: "Verified integration tests locally. Approve pending CI green and a short note in release notes about logprob availability differences across models." 
- Marta Ivanova: "Question about backwards compatibility for existing customers who rely on our previous streaming framing. Confirmed compatibility guard has been left in place behind the 'openai_compat_v2' toggle and we will flip after coordinated rollout."

Deployment plan: Feature gated under 'openai_compat_v2' config flag. Rollout steps: 1) Merge to main behind flag. 2) Enable on staging and run live-canary traffic for 48h. 3) Enable for 5% of production customers for 24h, monitor metrics (error rate, streaming disconnects, choice differences). 4) Gradual ramp to 100% if stable.

Related: Linked Linear tasks ENG-8243 (OpenAI parity epic) and ENG-8301 (streaming stability follow-ups). References: internal design doc (Linear link) and an internal benchmark note attached to the PR.

Notes: No breaking API changes for customers; behavior more closely matches OpenAI for edge cases (stop token slicing and logprob attachment). We've added explicit migration notes in docs/openai_compat.md and the SDK example to help customers who depend on exact framing semantics.
